headline: Pathology-preserving automated neuroimaging and SEEG analysis under clinical variability
label: Medical Imaging Representation Learning
summary: Recent preprints apply deep-learning registration, harmonized datasets, and automated localization to neuroimaging in epilepsy and brain metastases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning task-usable representations from neural imaging data while preserving clinically meaningful signal under acquisition variability and limited annotation. The melanoma registration preprint applies differentiable deep-learning deformable registration to align pathological brain MRI to atlases without lesion masks, preserving pathology for cohort-level analysis. The SEEG preprint reports automated electrode contact localization with 98.3% recall and 97.1% precision against expert labels in six patients, at about two minutes per subject. Omni-iEEG contributes a harmonized dataset of 302 pre-surgical intracranial EEG patients with 36K expert-validated event annotations and benchmark tasks, supplying shared resources rather than a new method. What is new is the emphasis on retaining lesion-level and electrode-level information through alignment and localization, rather than relying on a single shared objective.
